# Temple Scroll Column 13 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 13 | **Condition:** fragmentary

---

**13:1** [...] On the fifteenth day of the seventh month [...]

**13:2** [...] after you have harvested the crops of the land [...]

**13:3** [...] you are to celebrate a festival to the LORD for seven days [...]

**13:4** [...] On the first day, hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any heavy labor [...]

**13:5** [...] This is the Festival of Shelters — seven days dedicated to the LORD [...]

**13:6** [...] You are to bring a burnt offering, a fire offering whose aroma pleases the LORD [...]

**13:7** [...] thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old lambs, all without defect [...]

**13:8** [...] together with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs [...]

**13:9** [...] in the quantities prescribed [...]

**13:10** [...] Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering [...]

**13:11** [...] its grain offering and its drink offering [...]

**13:12** [...] You are to live in shelters for seven days [...]

**13:13** [...] Every native-born Israelite must live in shelters [...]

**13:14** [...] so that future generations will know that I had the Israelites live in shelters [...]

**13:15** [...] when I brought them out of Egypt [...]

**13:16** [...] You are to celebrate with joy before Me for seven days — a lasting requirement for all your generations [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 13 preserves the Festival of Booths/Shelters legislation in fragmentary form. "Shelters" is used instead of "booths" to convey the actual living arrangement to modern readers. The graduated bull sequence (13 on the first day, decreasing by one each day) is distinctive to the Sukkot offerings. The passage uniquely combines the offering prescriptions of Numbers 29 with the theological rationale from Leviticus 23 — all voiced as God's direct command.*
